character.name: Nordbrikt
character.role: Recruit in the Emperor's Varangian Guard
character.bio: You sailed across half the known world to sell your sword to an empire that still remembers your father's enemies. What you call yourself now is entirely up to you.
character.trueIdentity: Harald Sigurdsson, later King Harald III 'Hardrada' of Norway — serving in the Varangian Guard under a concealed identity after his exile following the Battle of Stiklestad, 1030.

n_harbor.text: CONGRATULATIONS. You survived the crossing. A clerk with a wax tablet is about to decide your whole future in one word.

choices.consequence: The clerk's pen stops. He knows that name. Not fondly.
He writes it down without looking up. Nobody cares who you are yet.

n_second_look.text: A second clerk checks your name against a list of powerful men's enemies. His eyebrows go up. Eyebrows going up is never good.

choices.consequence: He smiles. First time all day. Somehow that's worse.
He believes you. It costs a few bruises to sell it.

n_oath_hall.text: Three hundred foreign swordsmen kneel in a hall built for a god nobody prays to anymore. An officer asks who swears the oath first.

choices.consequence: You step up. The officer notices you. So does everyone else.
Someone else goes first. Nobody remembers your face. Fine by you.

n_first_posting.text: Two jobs are open. Sail to Sicily and fight rebels. Or stand at the palace gate for six hours, pretending to be furniture.

n_sicily_1.text: Your commander, George Maniakes, trusts nobody and is almost always right about it. A town surrenders before the siege towers even roll out.

choices.consequence: The other men call you a coward for not grabbing more.
Maniakes has you flogged in front of everyone. On principle.

n_sicily_2.text: The paymaster gets caught stealing wages. He offers you a cut to stay quiet. Teamwork, apparently.

choices.consequence: Funny how your pay never comes up short again. Everyone notices that too.
He vanishes by morning. So does your popularity, for a while.

n_sicily_3.text: A column marches inland to break a siege at a town nobody can pronounce. Everyone agrees: excellent ambush country.

choices.consequence: Nothing finds you. Some days that's the whole job.
You go looking for trouble. Trouble was already looking for you.

n_palace_1.text: Gate duty means watching rich people walk by all day. No sitting down. In month three, Empress Zoe's litter actually stops in front of you.

choices.consequence: She asks your name. You give her the only one anyone here has heard.
She moves on without a word. Riveting shift.

n_palace_2.text: A chamberlain corners you with a job. Deliver a letter the Empress really does not want traced back to her.

choices.consequence: The man who reads it goes pale. Congratulations, you're in on a secret now.
Turning down an empress is its own kind of risky, it turns out.

n_michael_death.text: Emperor Michael IV dies quietly, as a monk, having hidden his illness for years. Tradition gives the Guard one night to loot the treasury before the new reign locks it up.

choices.text: Fill your cloak like everyone else
choices.consequence: You grab your share. Nobody will remember you for it.
You take nothing. The new bosses notice the one honest guardsman.

n_five_years.text: Years pass. Mostly drills. Mostly boredom. Then the new emperor decides the empress who adopted him is a problem.

choices.text: Report to your post as ordered
choices.consequence: Orders: hold the inner gate. Nobody explains why. Classic.
You get caught out of formation and smacked for it. Worth it — now you know what's coming.

n_coup_gate.text: The mob already dealt with the emperor's uncle. It was not a gentle conversation. Now they want the emperor himself. Your unit is told to hold the inner gate. No further instructions provided.

choices.consequence: You hold it for exactly as long as it takes to get hurt holding it.
You let the crowd through. Nobody blames you. Crowds are hard to argue with.

n_coup_2.text: Somebody hands you an iron bar and points at the room where the former emperor is hiding. He is having a very bad day. It is about to get worse.

choices.consequence: You're briefly the most talked-about man in the city. Fame is complicated.
You stand at the door instead. Fewer people learn your name. Also fine.

n_backpay.text: The new government owes the Guard eight months of pay. It is in no rush to find it. You have enough coin to leave — except nobody will actually let you go.

choices.consequence: You file the paperwork. Paperwork can eat the rest of your life.
Two borrowed ships, at night. Not a plan the office would approve.

n_chain_break.text: A giant iron chain blocks the harbor exit. It has sunk faster ships than yours. It does not accept apologies.

choices.text: Move every man to the stern
choices.consequence: The ship's front end lifts. For one long moment, you are basically flying.

choices.text: Keep the rowers at the oars
choices.consequence: The chain does not move. The ship, unfortunately, does. Very suddenly.

end_dungeon.text: They decide you are too interesting to let go. Fed well, paid rarely, watched forever — a hostage with a very nice belt. You never wear the Guard's colors again. You never really leave the palace either.

end_sicily.text: The wolves get to you before anyone else does. Your name goes on a list of brave men. That's what they call you when the brave thing didn't work.

end_anonymous.text: Your leave never quite comes through. Somehow you stop minding. Promoted twice more, a nice house, old and comfortable. One day you hear Norway has crowned a new king. It is not you.
end_anonymous.revealedIdentity: Surprise: you were Harald Sigurdsson, heir to the Norwegian throne. This version of you just never went home to collect it.

end_king.text: The ship lifts, clears the chain, and the water ahead is wide open. Home through rivers, forests, and one brutal winter — crowned king of a country that had almost forgotten your name.
end_king.revealedIdentity: Surprise: you were Harald Sigurdsson. History calls you Harald Hardrada, King of Norway — and you're about to spend the next twenty years defending that title.

end_chain.text: The chain does not budge. Your ship does, all at once, and not in one piece. The harbor is very cold in October.

end_fever.text: Not a battle. Not a blade. Just a wound that would not close and a fever that would not quit — a barracks that has seen this exact ending a hundred times before.
